To import, choose Upload from file, pick the .ics file, choose which calendar it goes into, and select Import; Microsoft’s work/school instructions also show Save.

before: Microsoft suggests that if subscribing fails, you can import instead — accepting that you lose updates. In classic Outlook on the web, Microsoft also notes that if a correct internet calendar URL shows nothing, try removing it and adding it again with https instead of http.
after: Microsoft suggests that if subscribing fails, you can import instead — accepting that you lose updates. Its instructions for classic Outlook on the web also mention removing an empty internet calendar and re-adding its URL with https rather than http. That is a legacy web-client troubleshooting note, not a desktop Outlook command; use the publisher’s valid HTTPS feed address rather than inventing an address.

before: When the school moves an inset day on a Monday morning, the parent’s Outlook still shows the old date at lunchtime. after: When the school moves an inset day on a Monday morning, the parent’s Outlook still shows the old date at lunchtime. Such a delay is consistent with Microsoft’s figures; they check the school website and adjust plans. The imported sports-day entry does not follow subsequent changes from the school.
reason: A documented possible delay is not guaranteed diagnosis; imported events do not receive publisher updates, rather than universally never changing.

before: If a correct URL shows nothing, try re-adding it with https.
after: If a subscription is empty, verify the publisher’s current feed address and whether HTTPS is supported before changing or reconnecting it.
reason: Do not prescribe unqualified remove/re-add or guessed HTTPS URLs.

before: That is how import works: Microsoft calls it a snapshot. Remove the imported events and subscribe to the link instead if you need updates.
after: That is how import works: Microsoft calls it a snapshot. If you need later updates, subscribe to the publisher’s current feed and verify it first. Only then identify and deliberately remove any unwanted imported copies; do not delete unrelated events from the destination calendar.
reason: Avoid destructive blanket imported-event deletion before a verified replacement.
